difficulty.label: exam_prep
difficulty.rationale: Four short parts on one small 3-row table. Concept depth is moderate: enzyme activity peaks near an optimum pH, and the ±2SE intervals are used to judge whether means differ. Part A is a simple description of a trend (rate is highest at pH 7, lower at pH 4 and pH 10). Part B is one percent-change calculation: (17.7-5.9)/5.9 x 100, about 200%. Part C requires comparing the error-bar ranges (pH 4: 5.1-6.7; pH 7: 16.48-18.92; pH 10: 7.16-9.44). The ranges do not overlap, so all pairs are statistically different, and the answer is 'none'. A student could be misled into expecting some pair to be non-different. Part D asks the student to support the claim with data and interpret the non-overlapping error bars. The item changes representation only between the table's mean ± 2SE values and intervals, with no graph needed. The reading load is low, the calculator work is minimal, and the context is clear and within the AP Biology scope. This is typical of a full mock-exam free-response item rather than a basic recall exercise or an extension beyond the course.
